our_interpretation: The ordinary reading challenges the profitability of Cursor's enterprise customer business and offers some heavy users as evidence.
Profitability is read as subscription receipts less attributable service costs, consistent with the token-cost argument, rather than company-wide net income.
The ratio is read as actual cost to Cursor per subscription dollar. Retail API-equivalent usage is a different measure.

Because the statement describes ongoing economics without a reporting period, the latest completed calendar quarter before publication, October–December 2025, is used as a reporting proxy. This is an evaluator choice, not a period supplied by Zitron.
The accounting basis is estimate because the claimed ratios rely on customer reports rather than Cursor's financial statements.
Losses on selected users do not by themselves establish losses for their enterprise contracts or the enterprise cohort.
criteria.support_condition: Matching enterprise records show negative aggregate service contribution and document some enterprise customers whose actual attributable service costs reach two to three dollars per subscription dollar.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Matching-period enterprise accounts establish positive aggregate service contribution, contradicting the cohort claim; documented customer-level costs can separately test the stated ratios. Evidence about only one component does not automatically settle both.
